findings.title: Storage failures recorded as legacy metric
findings.body: In Create, when d.Storage.Create fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). No legacy call has happened, so this records the storage failure and storage duration under the legacy metric. Update has the same bug at line 129. These should call recordStorageDuration instead; otherwise storage error/latency dashboards are wrong and legacy failure counts are inflated.

findings.title: Delete metric uses object name as kind label
findings.body: Delete records a successful storage duration with d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage), passing the object name where the kind label belongs. This mislabels every successful delete metric and creates unbounded cardinailty/corrupted kind grouping. It should pass options.Kind like the other metric calls.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage metric
findings.body: The asynchronous DeleteCollection goroutine times the legacy call into startLegacy but then calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). Legacy latency/failures are therefore attributed to unified storage, and the legacy metric is never updated. It should call recordLegacyDuration.

findings.title: Async legacy writes can be canceled by request context
findings.body: All write methods start their background legacy call with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the original HTTP request context. The server cancels that context when the request handler returns, which can happen immediately after the method returns while the goroutine is still starting. The derived context is canceled too, so the legacy fallback write can be skipped or fail spuriously. The same pattern occurs in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a fresh background context with only the needed values.

findings.title: Independent async writes can reorder legacy state
findings.body: Each write launches an independent goroutine with no per-object sequencing. A rapid create/update/delete sequence for the same object can reach LegacyStorage out of order, e.g. a delete may complete before an earlier update and leave the object deleted in unified but still present in legacy, or an older update may overwrite a newer one in legacy. Because reads only use unified storage, this divergence goes unnoticed until fallback is needed. Legacy writes need serialization per object (queue/worker) or another ordering guarantee.

findings.title: Legacy Update no longer uses the object produced by unified storage
findings.body: The old implementation wrapped objInfo so LegacyStorage.Update received the exact object returned by Storage.Update. The new implementation passes the original objInfo to Legacy.Update, so LegacyStorage recomputes UpdatedObject against its own copy. If that copy is stale because prior asynchronous writes have not landed, or if unified storage defaulted/mutated fields, legacy can store a different object than unified storage, defeating the fallback guarantee. Capture res from Storage.Update and pass a wrapper using that object to Legacy.Update.

findings.title: Legacy write failures are no longer logged
findings.body: The background legacy Create path records only a metric and does not log errObjectSt. The same is true for Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection. Previously legacy failures were logged with object and error details. Now a failed fallback write is invisible in logs, making production diagnosis much harder.

findings.title: Delete tests do not mock or wait for async legacy call
findings.body: TestMode3_Delete success configures only Storage.Delete, but Mode3.Delete now asynchronously invokes Legacy.Delete. There is no legacy mock expectation, so testify's mock panics with an unexpected call if the goroutine runs. TestMode3_DeleteCollection has the same issue at line 284. More generally, none of the Mode3 unit tests wait for the background goroutine, so they can pass without exercising the legacy write path and can panic or race nondeterministically. The tests should set up the legacy mock, synchronize on the goroutine, and assert the legacy call.

findings.title: Mode 3 playlist tests assume synchronous legacy writes
findings.body: The new file and unified-storage mode 3 subtests reuse doPlaylistTests, which immediately reads /api/playlists after k8s create/update/delete and asserts the legacy API already reflects the change. Mode 3 performs those legacy writes asynchronously, so the legacy request can race ahead of the background write and make these tests flaky. The mode 3 cases need an eventually/retry check for legacy consistency or should not assert immediate legacy state.
